_comment: Public texts of the task page and the scorecard (site/build.py). `title` and `subtitle` replace task.json's title; `references` and `baselines` describe each design in one sentence (the internal notes of task.json and tests/expected.json are never shown). `new_design_reviewed`: the fingerprints (site/build.py `reviewed_hash`) of the README card's parts the page replaces with its own text, its opening and, with `new_design_checks`, its text on the commands, as last checked against the page; a README edit there warns (fatal under --strict) until the page is checked again.
title: IEEE 754 division, every format
subtitle: One divider for every exponent width and precision, rounded to nearest even.

references.fdivp: A word-level netlist for every format: a one-bit normalizer and P + 2 restoring division steps as generate loops, a shifter with a sticky bit, and rounding by an increment.
references.fdivp_newton: A Newton-Raphson divider: the first reference with its restoring steps replaced by a reciprocal, a quotient estimate and an exact correction, with a step count logarithmic in the precision; a second algorithm, not a competitive one.
references.fdivp_srt: A radix-4 SRT divider adapted from the CORE-V Wally processor: the restoring steps replaced by half as many stages, each choosing a quotient digit from -2 to 2 by comparing a few top bits of a carry-save remainder with table constants; the shallowest and fastest reference.

baselines.fdivp_d1: The natural parametric form, with `$clog2` and a logarithmic normalizer and shifter, checked by simulation on many formats but never proved.
baselines.fdivp_d2: A form of about 90 assignments, all inside what the proof tactics read, checked by simulation; the reference folds it into 34.
baselines.flat_binary16: A flat binary16 divider under this task's header: right at (5, 11) only, so it has no proof here.
